content: 1. When submitting a proposal for a new specification or an extension of an existing specification, it is essential to clarify whether the proposal pertains to joint FAO/WHO specifications or WHO specifications exclusively. For extensions of existing specifications, the source of the technical concentrate (TC) or technical material (TK) must be declared as the sole source. 2. For WHO specifications, confirm that the formulation and manufacturing process are identical to those used for materials evaluated by WHO Pesticide Evaluation Scheme (WHOPES) for efficacy. Additionally, ensure that the current production complies with the limits specified for active ingredient content and manufacturing impurity thresholds. 3. Provide any additional information that may facilitate the review and assessment of the application. Submit specifications in the standard format as a Word file (not PDF) and refer to the checklist provided in the manual. 4. Include original study reports detailing the physical and chemical properties of the active ingredient. Provide study reports supporting each parameter of the specifications for the formulated product. If FAO/WHO guideline specifications do not exist, validated test methods for measuring new specification parameters must be included. 5. Submit a letter of authorization granting WHO and relevant registration authorities access to national registration data for comparison of confidential data, such as manufacturing processes and impurity profiles. 6. Provide a concise description, supported by necessary data, of the manufacturer’s internal quality assurance and control schemes. Use the checklist to ensure all required data is included in the submission. 7. For the active ingredient, provide the ISO English common name, any synonyms, the chemical name (IUPAC and CA), CAS number (for each isomer or mixture of isomers, if applicable), CIPAC number, structural formula (including stereochemistry), isomeric composition (if relevant), molecular formula, and relative molecular mass. 8. Include studies and endpoints for the physical and chemical properties of the active ingredient, such as melting point, decomposition temperature, vapor pressure, water solubility, octanol-water partition coefficient, dissociation characteristics (if applicable), and degradation characteristics like hydrolysis and photolysis. 9. Provide data on the solubility of the active ingredient in organic solvents at room temperature for both pure and technical-grade materials. Specify the minimum active ingredient content and manufacturing impurity limits, supported by batch analysis data from at least five typical batches. 10. Detail relevant impurities, including their effects (e.g., toxicological or stability-related), and provide limits set by FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Residues (JMPR) or registration authorities, identifying the responsible authority. 11. For toxicological profiles, include data on acute oral, dermal, and inhalation toxicity, as well as skin and eye irritation and sensitization. Provide data on repeated administration studies (sub-acute to chronic), reproductive and developmental toxicity, genotoxicity, and carcinogenicity. 12. Confirm WHO classification by hazard and reference JMPR evaluations for toxicology, environmental fate, and ecotoxicology, if available. 13. For formulations, specify whether they are intended for public health or agricultural use, or both. Confirm that the formulation and manufacturing process are consistent with those evaluated by WHOPES for efficacy. List the main formulation types available and identify those for which specifications are sought. 14. Provide a list of countries where the formulations are registered and sold, or indicate the number of countries in each region or continent if the list is extensive. 15. Include physical properties as required by the manual, and justify any proposed deletions, insertions, or modifications to the guideline specifications. 16. For testing, provide at least two methods for identifying the active ingredient and one for identifying the counter-ion or derivative, if applicable. Include a validated method for determining active ingredient content and detailed methods for analyzing relevant impurities, along with validation data. 17. Reference test methods for physical-chemical properties and supply certified reference substances for pesticide active ingredients. Ensure that reference substances are accompanied by a certificate of identity, determined content, measurement uncertainty, and a reference to the analytical methods used. 18. Define storage conditions and expiry dates for reference substances, and ensure compliance with CIPAC guidelines for detailed information. 19. Use the glossary provided in the manual for definitions of terms such as active ingredient, impurity, formulation, and others. Ensure that all terms are used consistently and in accordance with FAO/WHO standards. 20. For equivalence assessments, compare impurity and toxicological profiles, manufacturing specifications, and physical-chemical properties of technical-grade active ingredients (TC/TK) from different manufacturers or manufacturing routes. Ensure that materials meet the same specification and present no greater risk than the reference material.
